title: Talent Attraction Scholarship Programme for Undergraduate Studies for 2026/2027

program_type: University merit scholarship for international students, awarded in two modalities (Type A and Type B) at admission to a bachelor's degree
funding_type: Full tuition + annual economic amount (Type A) / tuition-fee coverage only (Type B) - university-funded
administering_authority: Universidad de Jaén (University of Jaén) - Vicerrectorado de Internacionalización (Vice-Rectorate for Internationalisation), in collaboration with the Vice-Rectorate for Undergraduate, Postgraduate and Permanent Training

programme_action: Talent Attraction Scholarship Programme (Programa de Becas de Atraccion del Talento) - Undergraduate Studies, academic year 2026/27, Modality A and Modality B; call issued by resolution of 17 November 2025
description: The Talent Attraction Scholarship Programme for Undergraduate Studies 2026/2027 is an annual University of Jaén (UJA) excellence scholarship for international students entering a four-year bachelor's degree (Grado, 240 ECTS). The 2026/27 call announced 75 awards: 50 Type A awards carrying an economic amount of EUR 2,390 per beneficiary per year plus 100% tuition, 100% administrative fees and school insurance, and free Spanish courses for non-Spanish-speaking holders; and 25 Type B awards covering tuition, administrative fees, school insurance and the cost of Spanish courses but no economic amount. Selection is on the average mark of the qualification that grants access to undergraduate studies, on a scale of 1 to 10, with a minimum average of 8 out of 10 required as at 31 March 2026 and applicants required to be at least 18 years old by 1 September 2026. The award must be renewed year by year, subject to passing 90% of the credits enrolled in the previous academic year and, for non-Spanish-speaking holders, to completing the University's Spanish courses or reaching level B2.

programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Renewal is not automatic: holders must apply in the renewal call published every year. They must have passed 90% of the credits enrolled in the previous academic year (verified at the end of the second ordinary examination session in June and the second extraordinary session in July), and non-Spanish-speaking holders must submit proof of successful completion of the Spanish courses taken in the academic year immediately prior to renewal, or accreditation of level B2 in Spanish. Renewal covers the number of years in the curriculum, plus one additional year for engineering and architecture degrees in exceptional cases accredited and approved by the Commission.
programme_structure.intake: September 2026 entry (academic year 2026/27). The Type A economic amount is measured over a 10-month stay and is reduced proportionally for holders joining the University after 15 October 2026.

status_note: The 2026/2027 call is marked "Closed" on the official UJA page and its application window closed on 1 March 2026 at 23:59 peninsular Spanish time. The provisional and final award lists for this cycle have already been published on the UJA electronic notice board (SERC_12_2971482_2026_000704 and SERC_12_2971482_2026_000840). The scheme has run every academic year since 2016/17 and is re-called annually; UJA states on its programme overview page that applications are typically open between December and March each academic year. On that pattern the 2027/28 call is expected around November-December 2026 with a deadline around 1 March 2027, but the exact dates are published only when the new resolution is issued.
verification_type: Direct read of the official call page, the signed official call PDF (Annexes I, II and III), the programme overview page and the International Relations Office procedures page on ujaen.es, plus an HTTP check of the logo asset served from the same official domain.
verification_notes: The award name, the 75-award split (50 Type A / 25 Type B), the EUR 2,390 annual amount, the 100% tuition and fee coverage, the 240 ECTS structure, the 8/10 average as at 31 March 2026, the minimum age of 18 by 1 September 2026, the 1 March 2026 application deadline, the 15 October 2026 in-person registration deadline, the 31 October 2026 hard cut-off, the 90% renewal rule and the Annex I country list were all read from official ujaen.es sources. The signed resolution is dated 17 November 2025 and the page was published on 24 November 2025, so the 24 November 2025 date belongs to a genuine 2026/27 call and the cycle has not moved: the document was electronically signed on 2025-11-21T09:32:36Z. Two internal inconsistencies in the official material were found and are recorded rather than resolved: the English call page states the deadline as "March 1st, 2025" and the second payment as "from February 2026", while the Spanish page states 1 March 2026 and February 2027 and the signed resolution states 1 March 2026; and Annex II differs between the web page and the signed PDF, the PDF additionally listing English Studies, Telecommunications Technologies Engineering and Social Work. DELE and SIE are not named anywhere in the call; the Spanish requirement is stated as "certification of knowledge of the Spanish language" at application and as completion of the University's Spanish courses or B2 accreditation at renewal.

application_deadline.deadline_timezone: Europe/Madrid (hora española peninsular / peninsular Spanish time)
application_deadline.typical_application_window: Approximately late November/December to 1 March each academic year. UJA states on the programme overview page that "Applications period is typically open between December and March every Academic year"; the 2026/27 window closed on 1 March 2026.
application_deadline.application_period: Opened with publication of the call on 24 November 2025 and closed on 1 March 2026 at 23:59 peninsular Spanish time.
application_deadline.official_rule: Section 5 of the signed call: "Las solicitudes se presentaran hasta el 1 de marzo de 2026 a las 23:59 horas española peninsular a traves de la aplicación informatica disponible en la pagina web de la Universidad de Jaén." The English call page repeats the rule but with a typographical "March 1st, 2025".
application_deadline.deadline_warning: This deadline has passed and the call is closed. Do not rely on the English page's "March 1st, 2025" wording; the Spanish page and the signed 17 November 2025 resolution both state 1 March 2026. For the next cycle, watch the UJA international calls search page from November 2026 onwards.

programme_duration.official_range: 4 academic years / 240 ECTS for the funded bachelor's degree. The scholarship is renewable year by year for the number of years set out in the curriculum, plus one additional year for students in engineering and architecture in exceptional cases accredited and approved by the Commission.
programme_duration.renewal_note: Renewable annually for the full four years subject to academic results. A separate renewal application must be submitted in the call published every year. Renewal requires having passed 90% of the credits enrolled in the previous academic year, verified at the end of Ordinary Call II (June) and again at Extraordinary Call II (July). Non-Spanish-speaking holders must additionally submit proof of successful completion of the Spanish courses taken in the academic year immediately prior to renewal, or accreditation of level B2 in Spanish. The renewal call is separate from the new-entrant call: for the 2026/27 cycle UJA published a dedicated "Renovation Call for applications Talent Attraction Scholarship Programme for Bachelor's and Master's Degrees - 2026/2027" with a 15 June 2026 deadline.

funding.scholarship_type: Type A (50 awards): 100% tuition + 100% administrative fees and school insurance + EUR 2,390 per beneficiary per year + free Spanish courses + 100% of credit-recognition costs. Type B (25 awards): 100% tuition + 100% administrative fees and school insurance + cost of Spanish courses + 100% of credit-recognition costs, with no economic amount. University-funded, merit-based, awarded in competition.
funding.monthly_amount_note: No monthly rate is published. The Type A economic amount is stated as a single annual figure of EUR 2,390 per beneficiary per year, corresponding to a 10-month stay, and is reduced proportionally for students joining the University after 15 October 2026. It is paid in two instalments: 60% (EUR 1,434) after enrolment and registration, and 40% (EUR 956) from February once attendance at the first ordinary examination session is verified.
funding.travel_amount_note: No travel allowance is published. The only travel-related item is that in justified cases the Atraccion del Talento scholarship committee may authorise exceptional displacements between University campuses.
funding.institutional_costs: 100% of administrative fees and school insurance, plus 100% of the costs of credit recognition for students who request recognition, under both Type A and Type B. Recipients are additionally exempt from public prices for academic and administrative services for the 60 credits of first enrolment each academic year. Enrolling in more than 60 ECTS per year is at the student's own cost, and enrolments of fewer than 60 ECTS per year are generally not accepted. UJA's access page publishes the Andalusian Government-set registration price as around EUR 750 for a bachelor's degree.
funding.fully_funded_note: This must not be presented as an unconditionally fully funded award. Type A is a full tuition-plus-fee scholarship with an EUR 2,390 annual amount that also covers Spanish courses and credit recognition, but Type B carries no economic amount at all, so only half of the 75 awards come with money beyond fees. Neither modality publishes travel, installation, accommodation or relocation support, and the call does not state that the University pays for the health insurance the holder is required to contract. Payment is conditional on enrolment, in-person registration and verification of that insurance, and the Type A amount is reduced for late arrivals after 15 October 2026. Holding the scholarship does not secure a study place, which requires separate pre-registration through the Distrito Único Universitario de Andalucía, and amounts are repayable (reintegro) in the circumstances set out in the call.

tuition.conditions: Type A and Type B: coverage of 100% of the tuition fees for the credits required to pass the chosen programme (240 ECTS for undergraduate studies). The tuition fees for a full academic year of 60 ECTS credits are paid annually. Enrolling for more credits per year means the additional cost is paid by the student, and enrolments of fewer than 60 ECTS per year are generally not accepted. Recipients are also exempt from public prices for academic and administrative services for the 60 credits of first enrolment each course. The monetary value is not stated per award: UJA publishes the Andalusian Government registration price only as "around EUR 750" for a bachelor's degree.

monthly_stipend.note: Not published in official source. The economic amount is published as a single annual figure of EUR 2,390 per beneficiary per year for Type A, stated to correspond to a 10-month stay; no monthly rate is given.

travel_allowance.note: Not published in official source - no travel allowance is offered by this call.

installation_allowance.note: Not published in official source - no installation or relocation allowance is offered.

visa_support.conditions: Non-monetary support only. The call states: "La Universidad de Jaén dara el soporte necesario para el proceso de VISADO" (the University of Jaén will provide the necessary support for the VISA process). Holders must carry out all procedures needed to obtain the entry visa and, where applicable, legalise the documentation that makes up their academic record.

insurance.conditions: Both Type A and Type B: 100% coverage of administrative fees and school insurance, and 100% of the costs of credit recognition for students who request recognition. Type A: free Spanish courses for non-Spanish-speaking students. Type B: the cost of Spanish courses for non-Spanish-speaking students. Separately and additionally, every holder must contract a health insurance policy covering medical assistance (accident and serious illness insurance including temporary or permanent disability), death insurance including repatriation and/or medical transport of injured, sick and deceased insured persons, displacement of a family member in the event of hospitalisation or death, and civil liability with a minimum of EUR 40,000; a copy must be sent to talento@ujaen.es and the policy is verified before any payment is made. The call does not state that the University pays for this policy.

research_allowance.note: Not published in official source - no research allowance is offered by this call.

book_allowance.note: Not published in official source - no book or material allowance is offered.

equipment_allowance.note: Not published in official source - no equipment allowance is offered.

family_allowance.note: Not published in official source - no family or dependant allowance is offered.

accommodation_support.note: Not published in official source - no accommodation or housing support is offered. Holders must reside in the cities of Jaén or Linares as an essential condition of receiving the economic aid and of the insurance contract. Accommodation assistance is available separately through UJA's Welcome Center and Buddy Programme, which are not part of the scholarship.

bond.note: No bond or service obligation is attached: there is no requirement to work for the University or in Spain after graduation. Repayment obligations do exist: amounts received must be returned, with legally established late-payment interest where applicable, if the grant was obtained without meeting the required conditions, if the purpose for which it was granted is not fulfilled, if the obligation to provide justification is breached, or if any other obligation established in the call is breached. Unspent amounts return to the University of Jaén budget.

total_estimated_value.note: Not computed, in line with the contract. The call publishes no total award value. A Type A year comprises 100% tuition for 60 ECTS plus 100% administrative fees and school insurance plus EUR 2,390; a Type B year is the same without the EUR 2,390. Because tuition is published only as an approximate annual registration price (around EUR 750), no defensible per-award total can be stated, and a four-year figure would additionally depend on renewal at the 90% pass rate.

coverage_limitations: Only 25 of the 75 awards carry money beyond fees: the EUR 2,390 annual economic amount applies to Type A only, so a Type B award must not be described as a full ride.
Only 60 ECTS per academic year are funded. Enrolling in more credits costs the student the difference, and enrolments of fewer than 60 ECTS per year are generally not accepted.
No travel, installation, relocation, accommodation or housing support is published.
The call does not state that the University pays for the health insurance policy the holder is required to contract; only school insurance and administrative fees are explicitly covered.

The economic amount is reduced proportionally for holders joining the University after 15 October 2026, and the 40% instalment (EUR 956) is conditional on verified attendance at the exams of the first ordinary examination session.
Holding the scholarship does not grant a study place: admission requires pre-registration through the Distrito Único Universitario de Andalucía and is competitive.
Residence in Jaén or Linares is an essential condition of receiving the economic aid and of being a beneficiary of the insurance contract.
UJA publishes the bachelor's registration price only as "around EUR 750", so the monetary value of the tuition coverage cannot be stated precisely.
Exact benefit structure may differ in the next cycle: the number of awards, the amounts, the eligible-country annex and the reserved placements are re-set by each annual resolution.
eligible_applicants: Students with nationality in one of the countries listed in Annex I of the call, coming from foreign (non-Spanish) education centres or systems

Applicants who have completed, or are in a position to complete, studies in a foreign educational system that grant access to undergraduate studies at the public universities of Andalusia for the 2026/27 academic year
Applicants whose average mark is at least 8 out of 10 on the Spanish grading scale in those studies, as at 31 March 2026
Applicants who are at least 18 years of age by 1 September 2026
Applicants applying to one of the bachelor's degrees listed in Annex II, all of which run for four years / 240 ECTS
final_year_condition: This is an award for entering undergraduate study, so the relevant "final year" is the final year of upper-secondary education, not of a bachelor's degree. The call requires the applicant to have finished or to be "en disposicion de finalizar" (in a position to finish) a foreign qualification that grants access to undergraduate studies at the public universities of Andalusia for 2026/27, so final-year secondary students are eligible.
equivalent_degree_note: Annex III of the call sets out the recognised access routes. Holders of the European Baccalaureate or the International Baccalaureate may access undergraduate study provided they meet the requirements demanded in their country of origin for entry to higher education, even if the centre is in a country outside the European Union. Students from the education systems of EU Member States, and of China, the Principality of Andorra, Iceland, Norway, Liechtenstein and Switzerland, may access study on the same basis. Holders of a Baccalaureate or equivalent from other educational systems must apply to the Spanish Ministry of Education, Vocational Training and Sport for the corresponding homologation and/or convalidation of foreign studies and qualifications where necessary, and meet the university access requirements. Students with pre-university studies equivalent to the Spanish Ciclo Formativo de Grado Superior may also access, once the qualification has been homologated to the Spanish equivalent. Access itself is obtained through the pre-registration phases of the Distrito Único Universitario de Andalucía.
nationality_quota: Eligibility is limited to nationals of the countries in Annex I (Spain is not listed). On top of that, most of the 75 places are reserved for candidates routed through Spanish diplomatic education bodies. The reserved placements published in the call are: 10 Type A and 4 Type B for students selected by the Education Attache's Office of the Spanish Embassy in Moscow; 9 Type A and 6 Type B for students from Spanish language centres attached to the Education Attache's Office of the Spanish Embassy in Brazil; 3 Type A for students from agreement centres attached to the Ministry of Education of the Spanish Embassy in Argentina; 2 Type A and 2 Type B for students from agreement centres attached to the Ministry of Education of the Spanish Embassy in Mexico; 2 Type A and 2 Type B for students from agreement centres attached to the Education Attache's Office of the Spanish Embassy in Mexico; 3 Type A for the three winning schools in the secondary-education category of the "Colegio del Año en Español" contest run by the Education Office of the Spanish Embassy in Brazil with the Colegio Miguel de Cervantes of Sao Paulo; 2 Type A for students enrolled in the network of Spanish schools managed by the Education Office of the Spanish Embassy in Brazil who have passed the National Secondary Education Examination (ENEM) in that country; 10 Type A and 3 Type B for students of the Bilingual Sections Programme of Spanish or intensive Spanish teaching in Poland, Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Lithuania, Latvia and Ukraine, selected by the Education Department of the Embassy of Spain in Poland; 4 Type B for Kazakh students selected by the Education Department of the Embassy of Spain in Poland; 5 Type B for Kazakh students who, under the previously established agreement, could not obtain a place on the Business Administration and Management degree in English; 2 Type A for students from Tunisia selected on the terms of the agreement with the Spanish Ministry of Education and Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Tunisia; 2 Type A for students from Morocco selected by the Ministry of Education of the Spanish Embassy in Morocco or, failing that, from Spanish schools and institutes; 3 Type A for students selected by the Education Office of the Spanish Embassy in Bulgaria directly and through the Education Attache Offices in Hungary and Romania. Where there is no waiting list for an embassy or country with reserved places, those places are added to the general quota.
previous_award_restriction: A new undergraduate talent attraction scholarship, awarded to begin studies, may not be awarded to anyone who has already been a beneficiary of the undergraduate talent attraction scholarship in a previous call for applications, nor to anyone who is already studying the bachelor's degree for which they are applying at the University of Jaén. Holders renewing an existing award are not barred by this clause. The comparable master's scheme, the Talent Attraction Scholarship Programme for Master's Degrees, is a separate call and is not covered by this record.

Spain itself is not on the list, and applicants must come from foreign, non-Spanish education centres or systems. AMERICA DEL SUR Y CENTRAL - Argentina, Belice, Bolivia, Brasil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Haití, Honduras, México, Nicaragua, Panamá, Paraguay, Perú, Puerto Rico, República Dominicana, Uruguay, Venezuela. AFRICA - Cabo Verde, Camerún, Costa de Marfil, Gambia, Guinea Ecuatorial, Egipto, Kenia, Liberia, Marruecos, Mauritania, Mozambique, Namibia, República Sudafricana, Sahara Occidental, Senegal, Túnez. eligibility.residence_requirement: Holders must reside in the cities of Jaén or Linares; the call states this is an essential requirement for receiving the economic aid and for being a beneficiary of the insurance contract, except where the holder subsequently attends face-to-face mobility stays during an academic year. Registration in person at the International Relations Office, at Las Lagunillas Campus in Jaén or the Linares Science and Technology Campus, is a further obligation.
eligibility.age_limit: At least 18 years of age by 1 September 2026. Applicants who are minors at the time of applying for the visa or entering Spain must have a legal guardian in Spain, as the University of Jaén does not take responsibility for guardianship or for providing documents that would allow a minor to apply for a visa.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Completion, or being in a position to complete, of studies in a foreign educational system that successfully grants access to undergraduate studies at the public universities of Andalusia for the 2026/27 academic year, in line with Annex III of the call.
eligibility.academic_requirements: A minimum average mark of 8 on a 10-point scale, converted to the Spanish grading system, in those studies as at 31 March 2026. The transcript must show the GPA/average mark obtained in the country of origin; if it does not appear, the application is not accepted.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Minimum 8 out of 10 on the Spanish grading scale in the studies granting access to undergraduate study, assessed as at 31 March 2026.
eligibility.language_requirement: Where applicable, certification of knowledge of the Spanish language, required of applicants to any degree who do not come from Spanish-speaking countries, with the exception of the Degree in Business Administration and Management (English group). Where applicable, certification of English language proficiency, required of all applicants to the Degree in Business Administration and Management (English group) who do not come from countries where English is the official language. For renewal, non-Spanish-speaking holders must submit proof of successful completion of the Spanish courses taken in the academic year immediately prior to renewal, or accreditation of level B2 in Spanish. The call names no specific examination: DELE and SIE are not mentioned, and no band or score is specified.
eligibility.work_experience: No work-experience requirement is stated in the call.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: No extracurricular requirement is stated in the call; the selection criterion published is academic.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: No leadership requirement is stated in the call.
eligibility.financial_need: No means test or financial-need criterion is published. Selection is on academic merit; the economic amount of a Type A award is not reduced according to income, though it is reduced proportionally for late arrival after 15 October 2026.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: A new undergraduate talent attraction scholarship to begin studies may not be awarded to a previous beneficiary of the undergraduate talent attraction scholarship, nor to anyone already studying the applied-for bachelor's degree at the University of Jaén. Recipients of other UJA or Spanish scholarship schemes are not barred by this call.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Applicants must not already be studying the bachelor's degree for which they are applying at the University of Jaén. Applications are submitted by the student directly through the University's online application form, accompanied by the specified documents in PDF, and all communication is by the email address given in the application.
eligibility.health_requirement: Holders must contract a health insurance policy with the coverage specified in the call (medical assistance including accident and serious illness with temporary or permanent disability; death insurance including repatriation and/or medical transport; displacement of a family member in case of hospitalisation or death; civil liability of at least EUR 40,000) and send a copy to talento@ujaen.es. The policy is verified before payment is made.
eligibility.field_restrictions: The degree applied for must be one of those listed in Annex II of the call. If the selected degree is not actually taught, the student may enrol in another degree listed in the annex, provided a place is obtained in the pre-registration process. Annex II degrees are all four years / 240 ECTS.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: The fixed threshold is an average mark rather than a percentage: "Tener una calificación media mínima de 8 sobre una escala de 10 a fecha de 31 de marzo de 2026 en los estudios del apartado anterior (según la escala de calificaciones española)" - a minimum average of 8 out of 10 on the Spanish grading scale, assessed as at 31 March 2026. The mark used is the average of the studies that grant access to undergraduate studies, and the GPA or average mark must appear on the transcript.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: The average mark is taken from the qualification granting access to undergraduate study, so the underlying qualification depends on the applicant's education system. Annex III lists the qualifying access routes; applicants from systems outside the EU and outside the list of exempt states must obtain homologation of their qualification from the Spanish Ministry of Education where required. Renewal is subject to a separate, programme-level condition: passing 90% of the credits enrolled in the previous academic year.
selection_factors_may_include: Average grade of the teaching that grants access to undergraduate studies, on a scale of 1 to 10
Documented knowledge of Spanish, which gives preference for degrees taught in Spanish
Documented knowledge of English, which gives preference for applicants to the Degree in Business Administration and Management (English group)
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: Selection is academic only and no holistic review is published. The call states one academic criterion plus language preference, and gives no interview, portfolio, motivation letter, leadership, community-service or financial-need factor, and no weighting between the factors. Placement in a degree is additionally constrained by the pre-registration results of the Distrito Único Universitario de Andalucía, which the scholarship does not override.

english_requirement.test_score_note: English certification is required only of applicants to the Degree in Business Administration and Management (English group) who do not come from countries where English is the official language. The call names no examination, band, score or validity period, and publishes no minimum score of any kind. For all other Annex II degrees the relevant language requirement is Spanish, not English, so an English-language applicant must target the English-group degree.

language_of_instruction.bilingual_programmes: The Degree in Business Administration and Management is offered in an English group (grupo en ingles); all other degrees listed in Annex II are taught in Spanish. UJA also runs a separate scheme of courses taught in other languages (PATIE) that is not part of this scholarship.
language_of_instruction.language_note: Because 22 of the 23 Annex II degrees are taught in Spanish, applicants from non-Spanish-speaking countries must certify knowledge of Spanish, and non-Spanish-speaking holders must complete the University's Spanish courses or reach level B2 to renew. Type A holders receive those Spanish courses free of charge; Type B holders have the cost of the courses covered. Applicants to the English group must instead certify English proficiency if they do not come from an English-speaking country.

application_method.application_route: Direct application by the student through the University of Jaén's own online application form published on the call page. The call is not routed through a national agency, although selection is carried out "with the support, where appropriate, of the corresponding government agencies of the country of origin" and a large share of places is reserved for candidates selected by Spanish education attache offices.
application_steps: 1. Read the call, its Annexes I (eligible countries), II (degrees offered) and III (access requirements), published on the UJA international call page in English and Spanish.
2. Request from the home institution a transcript of records that shows the grades and the GPA or average mark; the application is not accepted without it.
3. Where applicable, obtain the Spanish or English language certificate required for the degree being applied for.
4. Complete the University of Jaén online application form and upload the documents in PDF format with the form.
5. Submit by 1 March 2026 at 23:59 peninsular Spanish time, and keep the email address given in the application under surveillance, since all communication is made through it.
6. Check the UJA electronic notice board for the provisional resolution, then lodge any claim within 10 working days using the form published in the call.
7. After the definitive list of awardees, substitutes and excluded candidates is published, await the individual notification by email.

8. If awarded, pre-register for the degree through the Distrito Único Universitario de Andalucía (foreign-access phase in March, or the ordinary or extraordinary phases) and obtain a place and enrolment.
9. Contract the required health insurance and send a copy to talento@ujaen.es.

10. Register in person at the International Relations Office (Las Lagunillas Campus, Jaén, or the Linares Science and Technology Campus) by 15 October 2026, and in any event before 31 October 2026, or the scholarship is deemed rejected.
11. If renewing, apply in the annual renewal call through Universidad Virtual, meeting the 90% credit pass requirement and the Spanish course or B2 requirement.

Transcript of records with the grades, showing the GPA or average mark obtained in the country of origin, requested from the home institution

Where applicable, certification accrediting knowledge of the English language

selection_process.decision_maker: University of Jaén, acting through the Vice-Rectorate for Internationalisation, which issues the provisional and final resolutions by resolution of the Vice-Rector. The Atraccion del Talento scholarship committee approves exceptional cases and authorises exceptional expenses. Selection is made with the support, where applicable, of the corresponding government agencies of the applicant's country of origin, and the education attache offices of the Spanish Embassies select the holders of the reserved places.
selection_process.selection_type: Merit-based competitive selection on the academic average of the qualification granting access to undergraduate studies, combined with reserved national placements routed through Spanish diplomatic education bodies.

selection_process.weighting_note: No weighting or scoring grid is published. The call states a single academic criterion - the average mark of the teaching that grants access to undergraduate studies on a scale of 1 to 10 - plus a preference for documented Spanish knowledge in degrees taught in Spanish and documented English knowledge for the English-group Business Administration degree. No cut-off score beyond the 8/10 entry requirement and no relative weight between criteria are given, so the outcome cannot be modelled.
selection_process.results_timing: The provisional and final resolutions are published on the UJA electronic notice board at https://sede.ujaen.es/publico/tablon. For the 2026/27 cycle the provisional list is dated SERC_12_2971482_2026_000704 and the final list of selected candidates is SERC_12_2971482_2026_000840. Claims must be lodged within 10 working days of publication. Awardees receive individual notification by email, and a five-working-day appeal applies to the later resolution that withdraws scholarship status for failure to register.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: A list of substitutes (waiting list) is drawn up on the same selection criteria as the awards. Where there is no waiting list for an embassy or country with reserved places, those places are added to the general quota. Vacancies arising from a withdrawal, or from failure to register at the University of Jaén before 31 October 2026, are first published as a provisional list of the students who lose scholarship status (both Scholarship A and Scholarship B), may be appealed against within five working days by writing to talento@ujaen.es, and are then awarded to students holding a Scholarship B in the order of priority obtained in the final list of awards.

selection_criteria.additional_factors: Documented knowledge of Spanish, which gives preference for degrees taught in Spanish, and documented knowledge of English, which gives preference for applicants to the Degree in Business Administration and Management (English group). In addition, reserved places are allocated through Spanish diplomatic education bodies and for specific school networks and competitions, and the University states that it will distribute the places across the fields of knowledge in the assignment process.

degree_outcome.degree_note: The Annex II list above is taken from the signed call PDF, which is the authoritative annex. The English and Spanish web versions of the call reproduce a shorter list of 20 degrees that omits English Studies, Telecommunications Technologies Engineering and Social Work; the web page also does not state the call's promise to publish the number of scholarships in each degree. If the degree selected by the applicant is not actually taught, the student may enrol in another degree from the annex provided a place is obtained in the pre-registration process.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: The scholarship covers 100% of the costs of credit recognition for students who request it, so recognition of prior credits does not cost the holder. Enrolment is set at 60 ECTS per academic year, with the fees for those credits paid annually; credits beyond 60 ECTS in a year are paid by the student, and enrolments below 60 ECTS per year are generally not accepted.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: 100% of the tuition fees for the credits required to pass the chosen programme (240 ECTS), with the fees for one full academic year of 60 ECTS paid annually, plus exemption from public prices for academic and administrative services for the 60 credits of first enrolment each course. Credits beyond 60 ECTS per year are paid by the student.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No application fee is published for this call, so no fee applies to the scholarship application itself. Pre-registration and enrolment through the Distrito Único Universitario de Andalucía are separate procedures governed by UJA and the Andalusian public price schedule.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: No scholar agreement or contract of study is published. Recipients accept the obligations set out in the call: pre-register for the degree through the Distrito Único Universitario de Andalucía, be admitted to one of the Annex II degrees, formalise enrolment, obtain the entry visa, be at least 18 years old on 1 September 2026, register in person at the International Relations Office by 15 October 2026, contract the specified health insurance, reside in Jaén or Linares, pass 90% of the credits enrolled annually, and meet the Spanish course or B2 requirement to renew.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Recipients are exempt from public prices for academic and administrative services for the 60 credits of first enrolment each year, receive free or cost-covered Spanish courses, and can rely on the Welcome Center and the International Relations Office for administrative support and a Buddy student. They may also apply separately for complementary aid run with collaborators of the University (Banco Santander's Santander Talent UJA programme and the Linares City Council) - these are separate calls with their own requirements and are not part of the scholarship award.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: No bond is attached and there is no obligation to work for the University or in Spain after graduating. Repayment obligations do exist: amounts received must be returned, with legally established late-payment interest where applicable, if the grant was obtained without meeting the required conditions, if the purpose for which it was granted is not fulfilled, if the obligation to provide justification is breached, or if any other obligation established in the call is breached. Amounts awarded but not applied for are returned to the University budget, and failure to register before 31 October 2026 means the scholarship is deemed rejected.

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: No motivation letter, personal statement or essay is requested by this call, so there is nothing to write for the award. The scarce resource is documentary, not narrative: effort is better spent on obtaining a transcript that explicitly carries the GPA or average mark, which the call makes a condition of acceptance, and on translating your average onto the Spanish 1-10 scale so that the 8/10 threshold can be verified. If you choose the English-group Business Administration degree, the equivalent effort goes into an English certificate from an anglophone-country-equivalent system.

common_mistakes: Applying with a transcript that does not show an explicit GPA or average mark, which the call rules out.
Assuming the scholarship guarantees a study place; pre-registration through the Distrito Único Universitario de Andalucía is separate and competitive.
Counting on receiving EUR 2,390 when only the 50 Type A awards carry it; a Type B award is fees only.
Confusing the 1 March application deadline with the 15 October in-person registration deadline for successful candidates.
Missing that enrolment is set at 60 ECTS a year and that taking fewer credits is generally not accepted, while taking more costs extra.
Applying for the English-group Business Administration degree without an English certificate, or for a Spanish-taught degree without a Spanish certificate.
Neglecting the residence requirement: the economic aid and the insurance depend on living in Jaén or Linares.
Assuming renewal is automatic after the first year; a separate renewal application and a 90% credit pass rate are required every year.

risk_flags.risk: The 2026/27 application deadline has already passed.
risk_flags.impact: The deadline was 1 March 2026 at 23:59 peninsular Spanish time and the call is marked closed, so no application is possible for this cycle and the record carries a closed status.
risk_flags.mitigation: Watch the UJA international calls search page and the programme overview page from November 2026 onwards; on the programme's annual pattern the 2027/28 call is expected around November-December 2026 with a deadline around 1 March 2027.

risk_flags.risk: Confusing the two October dates with the application deadline.
risk_flags.impact: 15 October 2026 is the deadline for selected candidates to register in person at the International Relations Office, and 31 October 2026 is the date after which the scholarship is deemed rejected. Neither is an application date.
risk_flags.mitigation: Track them separately: apply by 1 March 2026, and if awarded register in person by 15 October 2026 and in any event before 31 October 2026, since a failure to register converts the award into a Scholarship B vacancy.

risk_flags.risk: Assuming all 75 awards carry the EUR 2,390 economic amount.
risk_flags.impact: Only the 50 Type A awards include the economic amount; the 25 Type B awards cover tuition, administrative fees, school insurance and Spanish-course costs only, so a Type B recipient must fund living costs entirely.
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm the modality in the award notification before budgeting, and note that the amount is also reduced proportionally for joining after 15 October 2026 and is paid 60% up front and 40% only after verified exam attendance.

risk_flags.risk: Inconsistent publication across the official pages.
risk_flags.impact: The English call page states the deadline as "March 1st, 2025" and the second payment as "from February 2026", while the Spanish page and the signed 17 November 2025 resolution state 1 March 2026, and the Spanish page states February 2027. Annex II also differs between the web page and the signed PDF.
risk_flags.mitigation: Rely on the Spanish call page and the signed PDF for dates and annex content, and treat the English page's year references as typographical errors. Re-check the deadline and annexes in the next cycle's call before applying.

risk_flags.risk: The Spanish-language requirement on a Spanish-taught degree.
risk_flags.impact: 22 of the 23 Annex II degrees are taught in Spanish, and applicants from non-Spanish-speaking countries must certify knowledge of Spanish; renewal additionally requires completing the University's Spanish courses or reaching B2.
risk_flags.mitigation: Secure a recognised Spanish certificate before applying, or target the Business Administration and Management English group and certify English instead. Type A holders get the Spanish courses free, which is the cheaper route if you start without certification.

risk_flags.risk: The 8/10 academic threshold is applied on the Spanish scale.
risk_flags.impact: The requirement is an average of 8 out of 10 converted to the Spanish qualification system, assessed as at 31 March 2026, and an application whose transcript lacks the average is refused outright.
risk_flags.mitigation: Obtain the transcript early, verify the average is stated explicitly, and check the conversion before investing in language certificates.

risk_flags.risk: Residence and renewal conditions make the award conditional year to year.
risk_flags.impact: The economic aid and the insurance contract require residence in Jaén or Linares, and renewal requires passing 90% of the credits enrolled in the previous academic year, verified in June and again in July.
risk_flags.mitigation: Plan for four years in Jaén or Linares and enrol for at least 60 ECTS a year, leaving no room to repeat or reduce a course load without breaching the 90% threshold.

risk_flags.impact: Amounts received must be repaid if the grant was obtained without meeting the conditions, if its purpose is not fulfilled, if the justification obligation is breached or if any call obligation is breached, and unspent amounts return to the University budget.
risk_flags.mitigation: Keep enrolment, insurance, residence and academic progress records documented, and treat the annual renewal application and the June/July credit checks as hard compliance deadlines.

best_fit: A non-Spanish-speaking applicant from an Annex I country who has finished, or is finishing, a foreign secondary qualification granting access to university in Andalusia, whose average is at least 8 out of 10 on the Spanish scale, who is 18 or over by 1 September 2026, and who wants a full four-year bachelor's degree in Spain with tuition, administrative fees, school insurance and Spanish-language tuition paid for, and who is prepared to live in Jaén or Linares and keep 90% of credits each year to renew.
not_best_fit: Applicants whose country is not listed in Annex I - the list is closed and Spain itself is not on it.
Applicants who want a fully cash-funded award, since only 25 of the 75 awards come with money beyond fees and neither modality funds travel, housing or relocation.
Applicants who want to study in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia or anywhere outside Jaén and Linares, since the award depends on residence in those cities and attendance at the Jaén or Linares campuses.

Applicants who need the scholarship to guarantee a study place, since pre-registration through the Distrito Único Universitario de Andalucía is separate, competitive and outside the University's control.
Applicants who want to study through English entirely, since only the Business Administration and Management degree is offered in an English group.

Applicants who have already held an undergraduate talent attraction scholarship in a previous UJA call, or who are already studying the applied-for degree at UJA, since they are barred from a new award to begin studies.
Applicants who cannot commit to the full 60 ECTS annual enrolment and the 90% credit pass rate, since renewal, and therefore years two to four of funding, depends on it.
Master's applicants, who are covered by the separate Talent Attraction Scholarship Programme for Master's Degrees.

image.logo_verification_method: Fetched the asset directly from the official ujaen.es domain (HTTP 200, Content-Type image/png, 10,065 bytes). The same relative URL is the masthead mark of the University of Jaén across its own site - it is the target of the header logo link on this very call page and on the international-call search page - with the alt text "UJA. University of Jaén. Go to home." Decoded the PNG locally: 261 x 64 pixels, RGBA, with a transparent background, a near-black wordmark (RGB 34,30,32) covering about 29% of the canvas and a green accent (RGB 3,105,55). Zero pixels are near-white, so it is not a white-on-transparent wordmark and reads correctly on a light card. The awarding body for this record is the University of Jaén itself (through its Vice-Rectorate for Internationalisation), so the mark belongs to the awarding body.
image.image_usage_note: The PNG is the university's masthead mark on a transparent background and is legible on light and dark cards alike, since the wordmark is near-black rather than white. No photograph has been verified from an official ujaen.es source for this specific award, so image_url remains null rather than substituting an unverified campus image.

Cycle verification, as requested: the call page carries "Fecha de publicación: Mon, 11/24/2025 - 12:00", which is the publication date of a genuine 2026/2027 call, not a stale 2025 award. The signed resolution is dated 17 November 2025, the document was signed electronically on 2025-11-21T09:32:36Z, and the academic year it addresses is 2026/27, with a 1 March 2026 application deadline and a 1 September 2026 age reference date. All internal references are consistent with the 2026/27 cycle, so the record is filed as the 2026/27 cycle and the cycle has not moved. As at 2026-10-03 the next (2027/28) call has not yet been published, so any next-cycle dates in this record are expectations, not published facts.

Deadline accuracy: the exact calendar deadline is 2026-03-01 at 23:59 peninsular Spanish time, taken from section 5 of the signed call, so deadline_precision is "exact" and deadline_date is "2026-03-01".

The 15 October 2026 date in the assignment is the beneficiary in-person registration deadline at the International Relations Office, not the application deadline. Both dates are recorded, together with the 31 October 2026 hard cut-off after which the scholarship is deemed rejected.

The 75-award structure is confirmed as 50 Type A plus 25 Type B. The EUR 2,390 annual amount and the free Spanish courses belong to Type A only; Type B covers the cost of Spanish courses but no economic amount.

The 240 ECTS figure appears in the call as the total credits required to pass the chosen undergraduate programme, and every Annex II degree is four years / 240 ECTS. Only 60 ECTS per academic year are funded, and enrolments below 60 ECTS per year are generally not accepted.

The minimum average is 8 out of 10 on the Spanish grading scale as at 31 March 2026, taken from the studies granting access to undergraduate studies. The call adds that the GPA or average mark must appear on the transcript or the application is not accepted.

The minimum age is 18 by 1 September 2026, stated both as an entry requirement and as an obligation of beneficiaries, with a legal-guardian condition where the student is a minor at visa application or entry.

The renewal rule is a 90% pass rate on the credits enrolled in the previous academic year, verified at the end of Ordinary Call II (June) and again at Extraordinary Call II (July), plus, for non-Spanish-speaking holders, proof of successful completion of the Spanish courses taken in the academic year immediately prior to renewal or accreditation of level B2. Renewal requires a separate application in the annually published renewal call; for this cycle UJA published a dedicated renovation call with a 15 June 2026 deadline.

The Spanish-language requirement is not a DELE or SIE requirement. The call requires "certification of knowledge of the Spanish language" from applicants to any degree who do not come from Spanish-speaking countries, except the English-group Business Administration and Management degree, and requires English certification only from applicants to that degree from non-anglophone countries. No test, level, band, score or validity period is published.

The call is a Spain-hosted award restricted to nationals of the Annex I countries, coming from foreign, non-Spanish education centres. Annex I also lists Egypt, Iran, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Palestine, Saudi Arabia, Syria and the other Middle Eastern states among the eligible countries, but the award itself is hosted and taught in Spain in an allowed European region, so it is in scope on host-region grounds. Applicants should check the current annex each cycle, since the eligible-country list is set per call.
The Annex I country list is transcribed in full from Annex I of the signed call PDF. The web version of the call does not reproduce it, so the signed PDF is the cited source for the list.

The Annex II degree list in this record is taken from the signed call PDF (23 degrees). The web version of the call publishes a shorter list of 20 degrees, omitting English Studies, Telecommunications Technologies Engineering and Social Work. This discrepancy is recorded rather than resolved.

The selection is a single academic criterion - the average mark of the teaching granting access to undergraduate studies on a scale of 1 to 10 - plus a preference for documented Spanish or English knowledge. No interview, portfolio, motivation letter, leadership, community-service or financial-need factor is published, and no weighting between factors is given, so these are recorded as absent rather than guessed.

Award status: the 1 March 2026 deadline is earlier than 2026-10-03, so the record is filed as CLOSED in line with the contract's current-cycle honesty rule, while carrying the next-cycle expectation in status_note. The programme itself remains active and annually re-called, so verification_status is "active".

No service bond exists. Repayment (reintegro) obligations do exist and are recorded in funding_breakdown.bond and student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence, so the award is not presented as an unconditionally fully funded one.

The scholarship does not grant a study place. Admission requires pre-registration through the Distrito Único Universitario de Andalucía, and the call says so explicitly; this is recorded in coverage_limitations, risk_flags and degree_outcome.
